assembly: as world.json: copy ../r.-1.0.mca to dimensions/minecraft/overworld/region/ and ../level.dat to level.dat, then run every step below in order

histogram_after.why: the thaw box, counted exhaustively after it: a port that ate one block nobody sampled still fails here

note: each step is the operation to perform and the result it must report; fills, biome fills, connects and thaws run with keep_loaded, so nothing is released mid-script. The reported counts, the blocks read back, and the per-chunk NBT digests must all match. Digests are of the UNCOMPRESSED chunk NBT, so they are portable.

steps.why: a 5x4x5 platform, well inside one chunk
spans the border of two generated chunks
reaches into a chunk that does not exist; it must be reported, never invented
cell-aligned growth is reported, not implied
a bed lays both halves toward facing
a door lays both halves upward
stacked on the wall below, whose post changes
bare fence run, disconnected until settled
bare wall run: heights and post flags
two stairs whose corner is suppressed by the matching stair flanking them
...and a corner with no flank beside it, which does turn
settle the whole build, margin included
snow at three depths. Only layers=1 is a freeze product -- max_snow_accumulation_height defaults to 1 -- so 3 and 8 must SURVIVE and be counted as deep_snow_kept
a floor, so this ice is not a lid over air
the three tops that carry a snowy flag
already thawed: it must keep snowy=false and not be counted as cleared
a lid over nothing: the floating_water case
resting on stone: not floating
resting on snow the same thaw removes. The question is asked of the world as the call found it, so this is NOT floating water, and the answer cannot depend on which section the sweep reached first
snow_block is in BlockTags.SNOW and survives the thaw, so the grass under it stays snowy
powder_snow is in the tag too
deep snow, which the thaw also leaves, so this top keeps its flag as well
an ordinary layer, removed by the thaw below, so THIS top does get unsnowed -- the pair with the row above is what makes the vector discriminate
ice on water: the ordinary frozen lake, and NOT floating
cave_air is air: floating. A port whose air set is just minecraft:air misses this one
a lid at y=96, the first block of section 6, so its support is in the section BELOW. A port that looks for the block under it by wrapping inside the current section reads the wrong cell entirely
the same section boundary, but resting on the stone below it: not floating
the fence takes hold of the ice beside it
the thaw: rows 228, 230, 232 and 234
one block high, so the floating-water check has to read below the box to answer
reaches a chunk that does not exist: reported, never invented, and nothing frozen in the part that does exist

the ground row of z=238 ALONE. Every snow block sits at y=91, one above the box, so all four tops keep snowy=true. A port that answers `snowy` from the top's own state, or that only looks inside the box, unsnows all four here

now z=238 and z=239 whole. Only the top under the ordinary layer is unsnowed; the three under snow_block, powder_snow and deep snow keep the flag, because that snow is still standing when the thaw ends

crosses a chunk line (x -385|-384) AND a section line (y 95|96), with frozen blocks on both sides of each. Every other thaw here fits inside one chunk and one section, which leaves the local-coordinate clip untested: a port masking with `x & 15` instead of clipping against the chunk base reproduces those byte for byte and then thaws NOTHING for a real box. This is also the corpus's only chunks_modified of 2
deep_snow=True finally takes the layers=3 and layers=8 left standing at row 228, so the flag is not merely declared
unfreeze runs no aftercare, so this is the caller's job: the fence lets go of water
also the caller's job: taking a snow layer off lowers the surface
the legacy codec stores the bare id as given: level unsaid, which is its default, 0, the source
so the stair is waterlogged
flowing water waterlogs nothing: the stair displaces it and stays dry
nor does falling water, though its amount is the source's 8
seagrass is a water source in every state, as are tall seagrass, kelp and a bubble column: the fence takes its water
a coral asks is(FluidTags.WATER) && isFull(), an amount of 8: falling water waterlogs it
the conduit asks the same, so flowing water leaves it dry; it is wet by default, so dry is written out, as the game writes it
the small dripleaf is two blocks, and each half copies isWaterAt, any water: flowing waterlogs the lower, and the air above leaves the upper dry
the light block has no getStateForPlacement and is placed in its default state, dry, even into a source
a sea pickle dropped into air is placed dry; left bare it would read as its default, waterlogged, a source standing in the air
falling water waterlogs it too; the upper half takes the lower's facing
a coral is the conduit's rule: flowing water leaves it dry, written out
and falling water waterlogs the conduit
a double slab is a whole block: SlabBlock sets waterlogged false without asking the water
CampfireBlock sets lit to the opposite of the waterlogged it sets
unless the caller said lit
falling water is not the source a campfire takes: it stays as given, and lit
a waterlogged block holds a source
and a bare slab is dry, its default
level 16 is no water the game has: refused, nothing written
nor is a waterlogged that is neither true nor false
a double slab reads no water
nor does the light block
each half copies its own cell's water
the upper cell is read before the lower is written: no lone lower half
ground, a turned smoker and a soul campfire: two block entities, one kept
a whole section of air to one block collapses to a one-entry palette
two chunks never generated and two the game has not finished: nothing written
